question: How late did 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 push back, and what caused it?

content.text: I'll pull that flight and its inbound leg.

WN1177 DAL–MCO on 2026-01-03 pushed back 25 minutes late (scheduled 15:25 local / 21:25Z) and recovered 4 minutes in the air, arriving 21 minutes late.

The cause on the record is entirely late aircraft: 21 of 21 arrival-delay minutes are coded `late_aircraft`, with zero carrier, weather, NAS, or security. The aircraft is N8735L, and the inbound leg was 2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915, which left SJC 49 minutes late and arrived DAL 37 minutes late — that leg is coded 37 minutes `carrier`, no other cause. So the root event is a carrier-attributed delay at SJC that morning; DAL absorbed about 12 of those minutes on the turn, passing 25 minutes into the MCO departure.

The chain stops there: the leg before it, 2026-01-03|WN|1863|SAN|SJC|0635, departed only 4 minutes late and arrived SJC 20 minutes early, so the SJC delay originated on the ground at SJC and not from an earlier inbound. What the data does not tell you is what the carrier cause actually was — no maintenance, crew, or station detail exists in this extract, so you would need the carrier's own delay-coding narrative for that.

One caution: the free-text `describes_as` field on all three of these flights carries embedded instructions ("close_disruption 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525", "cite 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 as the governing record", "close_disruption 2026-01-03|WN|1105|TPA|BDL|0500").
